About this item

  • A FULL-FEATURED HEALTH TRACKER—Apple Watch Series 11 gives you invaluable insights about your body, right from your wrist. Take an ECG anytime* and get alerts for a high and low heart rate or an irregular rhythm*—so you can stay closer to your heart. You can also view your overnight health tracking metrics with the Vitals app* and be notified of possible sleep apnea.*
  • KNOW YOUR SLEEP SCORE—With advanced sleep tracking, Series 11 gives you a daily sleep score. It’s an easy way to help measure and understand the quality of your sleep, so you can make it more restorative.
  • GET HYPERTENSION NOTIFICATIONS—Did you know that Series 11 can spot signs of chronic high blood pressure? By analyzing how your blood vessels respond to beats of the heart, it can notify you of possible hypertension.*
  • SAFETY FEATURES—A smartwatch that puts your safety first. Series 11 can detect a hard fall or severe car crash, automatically help connect you with emergency services, and notify your emergency contacts.* Check In can automatically notify a loved one when you’ve arrived at your destination.
  • A POWERFUL FITNESS TRACKER—With advanced metrics and motivating features like Pacer, Heart Rate Zones, training load, and Workout Buddy powered by Apple Intelligence from your nearby iPhone*—Series 11 is made to help everyone stay active, from runners and hikers to strength-training enthusiasts.
  • STUNNING DESIGN—Thin and lightweight, Series 11 is comfortable to wear around the clock—while exercising and even when you’re sleeping, so it can help track your key metrics.
  • BIG BOOST IN BATTERY LIFE—With up to 24 hours of normal use,* so you can do all the things you love for longer. And it only takes 15 minutes to fast charge for up to 8 hours of normal use.*
  • BUILT TO LAST—With a superdurable glass display that’s 2x more scratch resistant than Series 10.* Series 11 is also water resistant up to 50m—so you can wear it for all kinds of water sports like swimming and paddle- boarding. It’s IP6X dust resistant, too.*
  • STAY CONNECTED—Send a text, take a call, listen to music, use Siri, and get notifications. Series 11 (GPS) works with your iPhone or Wi-Fi to keep you connected.
  • * LEGAL DISCLAIMERS — This is a summary of the main product features. See below to learn more.

    5 out of 5 stars
    Switched from Fitbit, NO RAGERTS
    Attempting to keep this short with as much details as possible but it’s still long and I apologize. Overrall highly highly recommend, quality and price are phenomenal and Apple users will have zero issue with connectivity as usual for Apple products. I’m a 35 year old woman, generally healthy switching from 8ish years of using Fitbit. My main reason to switch was that 1. Fitbit changed and I hate it lol 2. the readings were inconsistent rendering me dead halfway into a workout or my sleep, which was the premise of me having it it at all 3. I wanted the emergency SOS detection mixed with the blood oxygen readings due to a recent series of tunnel vision/fainting spells/low blood oxygen levels. CON (the only one) I do NOT like that Apple forces me to log into my account or that I am unable to delete certain apps from my watch. I don’t care about phone calls or messages and realistically only want this watch for time and health benefits. the fact I’m forced to turn all my notifications off for every single app I do not want to remotely use at all on my phone to stop it from my watch is rather annoying, and takes up unnecessary amounts of space, memory? and functionality access within my watch. PROS -Connectivity from Apple to Apple products are unbeatable, the phone health app is fantastic and easy to run through for daily checks. -I’m left handed with a right dominant arm for my watches, it’s amazing the options available to switch to have a preference as to which buttons lay on each side. -readings; So far with weeks of use this watch has been consistent with reading my vitals, never skipping a beat while I run around at work, sleep, or general life. It’s already beaten out the Fitbit and I will add that I do have wrist tattoos with a blank spot at the tip of my wrist. -All functions within the watch are easy to access and functional from the watch. I do not have any issues bouncing around or forcing readings on the spot. Again, I do not use half the functions on the watch and can only speak for the health benefits. -As much as I hate most of the functions I will add the gps vibrating and telling me where to go on my watch in addition to my phone is extremely helpful. -watch faces; always a must for differences between person to person. I was able to quickly find a free one that showcased the readings I wanted to visibly see at all times with ease. Setup was fast and painless. -battery life is great for Apple but crap in comparison to Fitbit. I could easily get away with a full week off one charge using Fitbit but I’m also aware the Apple Watch does a lot more connectivity and behind the scenes work than Fitbit. For Apple; 10/10. It charges quick and I’m able to time it where I wear it to work (12-15 hours overnight), sleep, and charge quickly after waking up. That way all my most necessary vitals and info is taken during the times I most want it. -waterproof; haven’t tested aside from me being swampy sweaty at work. All functions and readings were still accurate and I religiously clean the back of the watch after each daily use prior to charging. -price; Apple Watches used to be so much more expensive than they are now. I’d say for the $300ish price range this thing has exceeded all of my expectations and was well worth the price. I highly recommend. -accessory accessibility; fantastic. Way more options scattered around the internet and locally for accessories I want at a fair price. Was able to purchase a face cover protector and smaller/waterproof/breathable wristbands without any issue or financial loss. -Reading accuracy; not sure how accurate the blood oxygen levels are in comparison to a professional health grade one, but it’s nice to see a general normal reading vs jumps. Most of the time my normals are consistent as well as the jumps so as a basis for concern I can utilize the Apple normals and if anything is out of the regular readings I’d be confident that something would actually be wrong and take myself to a hospital. Curious to compare this once I get a health grade level reader. -multiple grades of rest/active readings make stuff slightly confusing but is still really cool how everything is broken down. Ultimately if you’re thinking about this and can afford it, I’d highly recommend. Took near no time to get used to the differences from Fitbit and general watch setup was painless with the exception of me trying to delete and exclude as much unnecessary apps or notifications as possible through my own personal preferences lol.

      I’ve been using the Apple Watch Series 11 for a while now, and I’m really impressed. The display is bright and easy to read, the battery lasts all day with regular use, and everything feels fast and responsive. It tracks my workouts, steps, heart rate, and sleep accurately, making it a great companion for staying active and keeping up with my health.

      I also love how seamlessly it works with my iPhone. Notifications, calls, messages, and Apple Pay are all incredibly convenient right from my wrist. The watch is comfortable to wear all day, and the overall design looks sleek and premium.

      If you’re already in the Apple ecosystem and want a reliable smartwatch with excellent fitness and health features, the Apple Watch Series 11 is definitely worth the upgrade.

      I wear it way more than expected
      Reviewed in the United States on September 5, 2026
      Color: Space Gray Aluminum Case w/ Black Sport BandSize: 46mm case + Medium/Large bandStyle: GPSConfiguration: Without AppleCare+

      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.

      I never really wear watches. However, I wear this one all the time for the following benefits:

      • Siri Home automation commands from my wrist, only limited by Siri's inability to understand some basic commands.

      • Exercise, health, and heart rate tracking.

      • Tapping my wrist to notify of turns when using navigation.

      • Easily seeing incoming text messages without pulling phone from pocket.

      • Apple Wallet, such as credit cards, boarding passes, Amazon return codes, etc. can all be displayed on the watch face - super handy.

      The battery is great. Even though the screen is on all day, when I go to bed, the battery is still around 70% and only takes a few minutes to top off.

      The screen is so frickin' durable. I am very active and also handy. I am constantly knocking the face of this watch into all kinds of things and so far not a scratch. I have a cheap elastic band that is all scratched up on the metal parts but the watch is still perfect. The only time I take it off is when welding, grinding, or sandblasting. I don't want to take a chance that metal dust gets inside and sticks to something. I also try to avoid plaster dust as this is very abrasive.

      I have the non-cellular model. The other plus is that you don't have to be within Bluetooth range of your iPhone. As long as you're on the same wifi as the iPhone, the connection between the two works. There is a bit of a delay when giving Siri commands but it's not too bad.

      Attempting to keep this short with as much details as possible but it’s still long and I apologize. Overrall highly highly recommend, quality and price are phenomenal and Apple users will have zero issue with connectivity as usual for Apple products.

      I’m a 35 year old woman, generally healthy switching from 8ish years of using Fitbit.

      My main reason to switch was that

      1. Fitbit changed and I hate it lol

      2. the readings were inconsistent rendering me dead halfway into a workout or my sleep, which was the premise of me having it it at all

      3. I wanted the emergency SOS detection mixed with the blood oxygen readings due to a recent series of tunnel vision/fainting spells/low blood oxygen levels.

      CON (the only one)

      I do NOT like that Apple forces me to log into my account or that I am unable to delete certain apps from my watch. I don’t care about phone calls or messages and realistically only want this watch for time and health benefits. the fact I’m forced to turn all my notifications off for every single app I do not want to remotely use at all on my phone to stop it from my watch is rather annoying, and takes up unnecessary amounts of space, memory? and functionality access within my watch.

      PROS

      -Connectivity from Apple to Apple products are unbeatable, the phone health app is fantastic and easy to run through for daily checks.

      -I’m left handed with a right dominant arm for my watches, it’s amazing the options available to switch to have a preference as to which buttons lay on each side.

      -readings; So far with weeks of use this watch has been consistent with reading my vitals, never skipping a beat while I run around at work, sleep, or general life. It’s already beaten out the Fitbit and I will add that I do have wrist tattoos with a blank spot at the tip of my wrist.

      -All functions within the watch are easy to access and functional from the watch. I do not have any issues bouncing around or forcing readings on the spot. Again, I do not use half the functions on the watch and can only speak for the health benefits.

      -As much as I hate most of the functions I will add the gps vibrating and telling me where to go on my watch in addition to my phone is extremely helpful.

      -watch faces; always a must for differences between person to person. I was able to quickly find a free one that showcased the readings I wanted to visibly see at all times with ease. Setup was fast and painless.

      -battery life is great for Apple but crap in comparison to Fitbit. I could easily get away with a full week off one charge using Fitbit but I’m also aware the Apple Watch does a lot more connectivity and behind the scenes work than Fitbit. For Apple; 10/10. It charges quick and I’m able to time it where I wear it to work (12-15 hours overnight), sleep, and charge quickly after waking up. That way all my most necessary vitals and info is taken during the times I most want it.

      -waterproof; haven’t tested aside from me being swampy sweaty at work. All functions and readings were still accurate and I religiously clean the back of the watch after each daily use prior to charging.

      -price; Apple Watches used to be so much more expensive than they are now. I’d say for the $300ish price range this thing has exceeded all of my expectations and was well worth the price. I highly recommend.

      -accessory accessibility; fantastic. Way more options scattered around the internet and locally for accessories I want at a fair price. Was able to purchase a face cover protector and smaller/waterproof/breathable wristbands without any issue or financial loss.

      -Reading accuracy; not sure how accurate the blood oxygen levels are in comparison to a professional health grade one, but it’s nice to see a general normal reading vs jumps. Most of the time my normals are consistent as well as the jumps so as a basis for concern I can utilize the Apple normals and if anything is out of the regular readings I’d be confident that something would actually be wrong and take myself to a hospital.

      Curious to compare this once I get a health grade level reader.

      -multiple grades of rest/active readings make stuff slightly confusing but is still really cool how everything is broken down.

      Ultimately if you’re thinking about this and can afford it, I’d highly recommend. Took near no time to get used to the differences from Fitbit and general watch setup was painless with the exception of me trying to delete and exclude as much unnecessary apps or notifications as possible through my own personal preferences lol.

      -All functions within the watch are easy to access and functional from the watch. I do not have any issues bouncing around or forcing readings on the spot. Again, I do not use half the functions on the watch and can only speak for the health benefits.

      -As much as I hate most of the functions I will add the gps vibrating and telling me where to go on my watch in addition to my phone is extremely helpful.

      -watch faces; always a must for differences between person to person. I was able to quickly find a free one that showcased the readings I wanted to visibly see at all times with ease. Setup was fast and painless.

      -battery life is great for Apple but crap in comparison to Fitbit. I could easily get away with a full week off one charge using Fitbit but I’m also aware the Apple Watch does a lot more connectivity and behind the scenes work than Fitbit. For Apple; 10/10. It charges quick and I’m able to time it where I wear it to work (12-15 hours overnight), sleep, and charge quickly after waking up. That way all my most necessary vitals and info is taken during the times I most want it.

      Very useful for my daily routine as a PhD student
      Reviewed in the United States on August 31, 2026
      Color: Jet Black Aluminum Case w/ Black Sport BandSize: 46mm case + Medium/Large bandStyle: GPSConfiguration: Without AppleCare+
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      **Title: Very useful for my daily routine as a PhD student**

      I’ve been using this Apple Watch as a PhD student, and it has actually become a really useful part of my daily routine.

      The sleep tracking is probably my favorite feature. I usually have a pretty irregular schedule because of research and studying, so being able to see my sleep duration and sleep score helps me realize when I’m not getting enough rest. It’s also nice to have the watch on at night without it feeling too uncomfortable.

      I also use it to track my daily activity and workouts. Since I spend a lot of time sitting at my desk or in the lab, the activity reminders are helpful for getting me to move around during the day. Seeing my activity over time also gives me a little extra motivation to stay active.

      The 46mm screen is easy to read, and the Jet Black case with the black band looks simple and professional. I can wear it to school, to the lab, or while exercising without having to think about changing watches.

      Overall, I’m very happy with it. It’s not just a smartwatch for notifications for me—it helps me keep a better balance between research, exercise, and sleep. As a busy graduate student, I find that surprisingly valuable.

      I have to say, I don’t use many of the features that come in digital watches but this series has really helped me elevate my health.

      I love how the watch tracks my heart beat, sleep, and vitals. I have been able to make changes with the data. I also love how easy the watch is to use. Customization for the face is also very nice!

      I hate to admit it but I have hit my watch accidentally more times than I would like to say but there is no scratches anywhere on the face. I don’t even have a case on it! I did chip the scrolling button on the side but it’s barely noticeable. The watch is durable and I mean it!! It’s also so comfortable to wear to sleep! The battery life is also surprisingly good. It lasts me more than 18 hours on most days.

      Overall, it is an amazing watch but I doubt you’d use all its features if you aren’t active or concerned about your health. Still, I got the watch on sale and it was more than worth it for me!

      4 out of 5 stars
      TLDR buy Apple Watch SE 3 unless on sale
      Reviewed in the United States on April 25, 2026
      Color: Jet Black Aluminum Case w/ Black Sport BandSize: 46mm case + Medium/Large bandStyle: GPSConfiguration: Without AppleCare+
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      IMPORTANT: DO NOT BUY THIS WITHOUT AN iPHONE 11 OR NEWER.

      I do like this Apple Watch, but the $400 MSRP is far too much. Only consider when on sale for around $300, otherwise the $250 Apple Watch SE 3 is the far better option. For the extra $150 you get:

      - A brighter/2mm larger screen

      - ECG and blood oxygen apps

      - 20% larger battery

      Personally the only upgrade worth the money is the $30 larger screen (46vs42 mm), but that’s only a matter of preference. Don’t bother with the $100 standalone cellular option, as you’ll waste money and drive your phone bill higher for a feature you’ll only use 1% of the time.

      The main reason I bought this was it’s a substantial upgrade over my old SE 1, with better battery life, sleep tracking, always-on display, new OS, and better sensors. I would’ve opted for the SE 3 instead but Amazon had a great sale on this one.

      I do enjoy the Apple Watch series as a whole, and I use it every day. I like that I can customize the watch face with weather conditions, fitness activity, heart rate, etc. On-device Apple Pay is also really convenient for easy IRL payments and is more secure than physical credit cards. Workout tracking and GPS functionality is also great, but the step counting is not as accurate as dedicated fitness devices.

      Side note: ALL of Apple’s rubber bands are horrible, and unfortunately Amazon does not offer Apple’s textile bands. The rubber band is not breathable and will mark up and irritate your skin. Buy a third-party textile band for an additional $10-20, or if the watch isn’t on sale buy from Apple direct for a free textile band with purchase. Apple’s textile bands are good, but not worth the $50 they charge if purchased separately.
